A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same TBA research, and their text, equations, figures, tables and appendices support reliable comparison. Retained material can be matched across renumbering and relocation, including the original ablations and red-teaming table.

before.justification: Section 5 and Appendices A–C report original TBA experiments on GSM8K, TL;DR summarization and automated red-teaming, including scaling and hyperparameter ablations.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds original MATH/Countdown evaluations, GRPO benchmarking and component ablations in Section 6 and Appendices C–E.

M1.justification: v2 retains buffer-based TBA and introduces TBA′ in PRIME-RL: fixed-staleness training without the original replay sampling, constant beta with periodic reference-policy resetting, and clipped importance sampling. Appendix D also evaluates an IcePop-masking variant. These additions change the update and data-use procedures, rather than merely documenting another implementation.

E1.justification: v1 evaluates GSM8K, TL;DR summarization and GPT-2/Llama red-teaming. v2 retains that coverage and adds MATH training with MATH-500 evaluation and generated Countdown problems for TBA′ (Section 6; Appendix C), substantially expanding reasoning-task coverage.

E2.justification: v2 adds an evaluated synchronous GRPO baseline on GSM8K, Dr. GRPO and IcePop comparisons on MATH/Countdown, and a Kimi-K2-style objective comparison on Countdown (Figures 1, 6, 10 and 11). These extend the actual comparator set beyond v1; CISPO's appearance in gradient comparisons alone is not counted as a separate evaluated baseline.

E3.justification: New TBA′ protocols use Qwen2.5-7B-Base and Qwen3-4B-Instruct-2507, 2- and 10-step staleness, 400/500 training steps, and a 9,000/1,000 Countdown training/test split (Section 6; Appendix C; Table 4). v2 also expands PFT comparisons to asynchronous settings and tests K=20 versus 40 completions at fixed batch size on GSM8K. Original TBA settings are largely retained.

E4.justification: The original GSM8K and TL;DR ablations remain as Figures 12 and 14. v2 adds tests of disabling importance sampling or reference resetting, replacing clipping with masking, and robustness to increased staleness (Figures 6–10). Table 5 and Appendix E.1 additionally examine completion-count effects, GRPO training dynamics and unsuccessful asynchronous GRPO configurations.

E5.justification: Appendix B.3 newly specifies three runs per GPT-2 red-teaming configuration, where v1 only stated multiple runs. v2 also reports standard deviations for the completion-count ablation and displays separate Countdown replicates. Existing mean/standard-error reporting remains; the newly disclosed red-teaming count does not establish an increase in runs.

E6.justification: v2 newly reports GRPO's 49.05% GSM8K accuracy and the K=20/40 ablation accuracies of 54.61%/54.89%. Figures 6–11 add TBA′ results showing greater stability than Dr. GRPO/IcePop at 10-step staleness and similar Countdown performance to Kimi-K2-style training. Table 1 adds asynchronous baseline scores. The original 54.6% TBA headline result and relocated red-teaming table remain unchanged.

T1.justification: v1 provides the TB/VarGrad objectives without the later gradient analysis. v2 adds Section 3.3, Appendix A's derivation, and Appendix D's formal gradient comparisons with Proximal RLOO, CISPO, Dr. GRPO and Kimi-K2-style objectives. It establishes the stated on-policy connection to mean-baseline REINFORCE with KL-regularized rewards and qualifies that connection off-policy.

C1.justification: The central claim of faster asynchronous post-training with competitive or better performance remains. v2 narrows the abstract's categorical claim that on-policy algorithms are inherently incompatible with replay buffers to a lack of natural robustness to diversified replay data. It also foregrounds robustness as asynchrony increases and applicability through 7B models, without replacing the main contribution.

C2.justification: Beyond v1's exploration and replay-based explanations, v2 interprets the new ablations through KL regularization, reference resetting and task-dependent benefits of importance sampling. Appendix D discusses the stability/adherence tradeoff controlled by beta and reset frequency, explains differences from Kimi's reference policy, and identifies reward-hacking settings as an untested direction. These substantially expand the mechanism discussion and applicability qualifications.

D1.justification: v2 newly provides a code-repository link, PRIME-RL implementation information, TBA′ hyperparameters in Table 4, and detailed GRPO reproduction settings in Appendix E.1, including TRL 0.17.0, DeepSpeed ZeRO Stage 2 and 4×A100 80 GB hardware. The original TBA hyperparameter tables are largely retained and renumbered.

R1.justification: v2 substantially expands positioning against recent asynchronous RL objectives and systems. Sections 2–3 and Appendix D distinguish near-on-policy approaches, connect GFlowNets with maximum-entropy RL/path consistency, and discuss ProRL-style resetting, Dr. GRPO, CISPO, IcePop and Kimi K1.5/K2. This adds substantive relationships and novelty qualifications beyond v1's related-work discussion.

P1.justification: v2 revises the abstract and introduction, reorganizes the method overview around two implementations, combines metric/baseline paragraphs and subdivides the preliminaries. Appendix organization and discussion headings also change. Much of the retained experimental prose remains close to v1; the substantial scientific additions do not amount to a pervasive rewrite of existing text.

P2.justification: v2 adds Figures 6–11 and 13 and Tables 4–5, expands Table 1 into staleness blocks, and adds GRPO to Figure 1. The original red-teaming Table 2 moves to Appendix G as Table 6, while original ablation figures become Figures 12 and 14. NeurIPS formatting also changes typography, captions and page layout.

improvement.justification: v1 demonstrates useful speedups but provides limited objective-level analysis and component isolation. v2 substantially strengthens that foundation through gradient derivations, controlled resetting/importance-sampling ablations, modern baseline comparisons and larger-model experiments, supported by additional implementation details. The Kimi comparison also usefully qualifies the method's positioning. Larger-model evidence concerns the new TBA′ variant, and uncertainty reporting remains uneven, but the gains in explanatory support and empirical scrutiny are substantial.
